name: Arizona

sales.rateNote: Arizona levies a transaction privilege tax (TPT), a tax on the vendor for the privilege of doing business, usually passed on to buyers. The 5.6% state retail rate is the 5% base rate (A.R.S. 42-5010) plus a voter-approved 0.6% education increment. Counties and cities add their own TPT.

local.levies: county excise taxes and city/town transaction privilege taxes, all collected by ADOR; some cities apply tiered rates on single items above a set price
local.capNote: Cities must follow the state retail rules (A.R.S. 42-6017) but may still tax food for home consumption.

groceries.note: Food for home consumption sold by grocery-type retailers is exempt from state TPT (A.R.S. 42-5102); food consumed on the premises is taxable. Cities and towns may still levy their TPT on food sales.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable under the retail classification; Arizona has no clothing exemption.

otherRates.note: State base rate for hotels and short-term lodging (A.R.S. 42-5010(A)(2)), before the education increment and local taxes.
State base rate for the mining classification.
No state TPT on commercial leases; cities may tax them.

sales.holidayNote: Arizona has no sales tax holiday.

useTax.note: State use tax on items bought from out-of-state retailers without Arizona tax is levied at the same rate as the retail TPT (A.R.S. 42-5155), including the 0.6% increment.

facts.text: Arizona's 'sales tax' is legally a transaction privilege tax on the seller, not on the buyer, though sellers may pass it on.
Prescription drugs are exempt from both state and city TPT.
Groceries are exempt from state TPT, but cities and towns may tax food sold for home consumption.
Since January 1, 2025, no city or town may tax residential rents (A.R.S. 42-6004(H)).
Some cities use tiered rates: a different rate on single items priced above a threshold, either on the whole item or on the portion over it.
City rate changes take effect only after a 60-day notice period agreed between ADOR and the municipalities.
Nonresidents buying a car in Arizona pay a reduced state rate if their home state's vehicle tax is lower than Arizona's 5.6%.

property.levied: County, city, school district, community college and special district levies, billed and collected by the county treasurer; primary taxes on the limited property value (LPV).

assessment.text: Owner-occupied homes (class three) are assessed at 10% of limited property value. The LPV may rise by at most 5% a year and never above full cash value. Commercial property (class one) is assessed at 15.5% in 2026, falling to 15% from 2027.

homestead.name: Homeowner rebate (additional state aid to education)
homestead.text: On owner-occupied homes the state pays part of the school district primary tax (50% of the qualifying rate, limited to half the district's primary rate), reducing each home's bill by up to $600. Separately, primary taxes on a home cannot exceed 1% of its limited value.
homestead.applyBy: Applied by the county on owner-occupied (primary residence) classification.

otherRelief.name: Widow/widower and disability exemption
otherRelief.text: $4,188 of assessed value (statutory base, indexed each year) for eligible widows, widowers and totally disabled residents within income and assessment limits.

otherRelief.name: 100% disabled veteran exemption
otherRelief.text: The primary residence of a veteran rated 100% service-connected disabled (or unemployable) is fully exempt, as is that of the surviving spouse.

otherRelief.name: 1% residential cap
otherRelief.text: Primary taxes on residential property may not exceed 1% of its limited value (bonds and voter overrides excluded).

dueDates.text: First half due October 1, delinquent after November 1 at 5 p.m.; second half due March 1, delinquent after May 1 at 5 p.m. Bills of $100 or less are due in full October 1. No interest is charged if the full year is paid by December 31.

facts.text: Limited property value rises at most 5% a year (A.R.S. 42-13301), whatever the market does.
The Arizona Constitution caps primary taxes on a home at 1% of its limited value.
The commercial assessment ratio has been cut step by step from 25% in 2005 to 15.5% in 2026 and 15% from 2027.
Residential rentals (class four) are assessed at the same 10% ratio as owner-occupied homes but do not get the homeowner rebate.
Late property taxes bear 16% simple interest a year.
